section.title: REVIEW OF PROPOSAL COMPONENTS
section.description: The proposal is separated into three sections.

question.text: • Section 2.1 characterizes the aquifer formation that each groundwater well in the West taps and

json.answer: compares well construction patterns before and after the establishment of regulatory controls.

question.text: • Section 2.2 estimates groundwater components of the water budget (withdrawals and consumption)

json.answer: yearly (2016-2021) at the field scale.

question.text: • Section 2.3 integrates research and education through the Scientist Spotlight and Hydrologic

json.answer: Sciences Workshops.

question.text: The PI and PhD student will be responsible for all data-related activities including: collection,

json.answer: documentation and metadata description, quality control, storage and backup, archiving, and sharing.

question.text: The project will result in new sets of data, code, and tools. These outputs include: (a) source code to

json.answer: quality control, collate, and merge datasets, (b) open source models and budgets in R and/or python, and

question.text: (c) sharable instructional materials (Scientist Spotlight activities and workshop materials).

json.answer: Available data will be systematically reviewed and downloaded. These data are likely

question.text: available in the form of Microsoft Access files or Microsoft Excel spreadsheets; shapefiles or raster files;

json.answer: or text files or comma-delimited files. A multi-tier storage and quality assurance methodology will be

question.text: adopted and will likely evolve as new datasets provide for challenging formats and organization.

json.answer: Datasets will be produced in Sections 2.1-2.3 of the proposal. These datasets will be

question.text: formatted and shared in an open format (e.g., CSV) or in illustrator files (i.e., cross sections).

json.answer: The data will be shared along with a README.txt, which will describe all files, their relationships,

question.text: naming conventions, etc. Data elements and attributes will be described following ISO 19115

json.answer: specifications and metadata schema and standards in Hydrology (e.g., following any establish standards

question.text: of the Water Information Coordination Program’s Open Water Data Initiative (Larsen et al., 2016)) to

json.answer: allow for better interpretability and interoperability. Code and scripts produced in R and/or python will be

question.text: documented for reproducibility purposes. The metadata for the codes will include: (1) description of the

json.answer: functions required to operate the analyses; (2) description of input parameters and outputs; and (3) test

question.text: case, files and plots documenting the expected response of the model (Section 2.1) to a standard set of

json.answer: input parameters. Documentation will focus on the description of the functions, input parameters, outputs,

question.text: the format of input data, instructions to run the model, and instructions to export the results. The outputs

json.answer: will be stored in CSV format with a metadata document describing the data structure of the output data.

question.text: Raw data:

json.answer: Detailed information about how the data were obtained, including detailed contact information

question.text: or websites for direct download and citations to all datasets will be provided to allow for accessibility and

json.answer: correct attribution to original collectors. All methodological procedures for data quality control and

question.text: aggregation will be described in the data documentation. This information will be provided in the form of

json.answer: supplementary documentation for publications, in the README.txt file, and at the repository (record-

question.text: level). All sharable raw data and the processed data will be archived in Dryad, https://datadryad.org, the

json.answer: agnostic open access repository backed by UCSB and the California Digital Library (CDL), which

question.text: implements the latest best practices in data curation, publication, citation, and archival. Dryad assigns

json.answer: Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs) to deposited datasets and makes data discoverable through such services

question.text: as the Thomson-Reuters Data Citation Index, Scopus, and Google Dataset Search. All data in Dryad is

json.answer: publicly accessible and released under a CC0 license. Data will be linked to publications and vice versa

question.text: through DOIs.

json.answer: All scripts and code will be archived in supplementary information

question.text: appendices in publications as well as uploaded to Zenodo through the Dryad repository submission

json.answer: process along with the sharable raw and processed data in order to allow citations and a better connection

question.text: to the research data curation and publication processes.

json.answer: All scientist spotlight biographies, assignments, and open-access readings will be

question.text: posted to an online Dashboard associated with the PI’s website, which is updated bi-monthly.

json.answer: Workshop material will be shared with UCSB’s Diversity Committee through

question.text: Google Drive; if workshop materials are fully supported by the Diversity Committee, these materials will

json.answer: also be shared through eSholarship for broader dissemination.

question.text: The PI is committed to publishing in open access journals. The UC is currently leading initiatives to assist

json.answer: faculty in paying for open access journals.

section.title: POLICIES AND PROVISIONS FOR RE-USE, RE-DISTRIBUTION

json.answer: All data deposited at Dryad will be publicly available under a CC0 license, meaning that others may

question.text: freely build upon, enhance and reuse the works for any purposes without restriction under copyright or

json.answer: database law. CC0 does not exempt those who reuse the data from following community norms for

question.text: scholarly communication, i.e., reusing the data in a way that is mindful of its limitations and citing the

json.answer: original data authors.

section.title: PLANS FOR ARCHIVING AND PRESERVATION OF ACCESS

json.answer: UCSB Box will be used as the primary means to store and back up all collected input, generated output

question.text: data sets and code, and educational materials over the course of the project and prior to data sharing. Box

json.answer: provides encryption of data at rest and in-transit, detailed logging of file actions, two-factor

question.text: authentication, and access review of collaborators. Data will be accessed using Box Drive, which requires

json.answer: full disk encryption, firewall, and an antivirus software in order to install on a local computer.

question.text: At the end of the project, all shareable data accompanied by the appropriate documentation, metadata, and

json.answer: code will be deposited into Dryad for long-term storage, preservation and accessibility. Deposits

question.text: submitted to Dryad are curated prior to public release to conform with quality standards and enable future

json.answer: reuse.

question.text: The source code for the research and education components (Sections 2.1, 2.2., and 2.3) will be saved,

json.answer: stored, and backed up on the UCSB Box. A copy of the code will also be submitted with each of the three

question.text: planned publications. After the evaluation and refinement of the developed datasets and tools and once

json.answer: the research is completed and published, the final version of the tools and the documentation will be

question.text: shared on the UCSB’s Dryad Data Repository. The final shareable instructional and teaching materials

json.answer: will also be shared via on a publicly accessible webpage (Scientist Spotlight) and UCSB Google Drive

question.text: (workshop materials) and Dryad in pdf format.
